statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is exactly the list of all distinct sequences s of 64-bit signed integers such that: (a) 2 <= len(s); (b) s is non-decreasing, meaning s[k] <= s[k+1] for every k with 0 <= k < len(s)-1; and (c) s is a subsequence of nums, meaning there exist indices j_0, ..., j_{len(s)-1} with 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{len(s)-1} < len(nums) and nums[j_t] = s[t] for every t with 0 <= t < len(s). The phrase exactly means: every entry r[q] satisfies (a)-(c); every sequence s satisfying (a)-(c) equals some entry r[q] (same length and same values at each index); and no two entries of r are equal as sequences. The order of the entries of r is arbitrary and unconstrained.
preconditions: len(nums) is between 1 and 15 inclusive, and -100 <= nums[i] <= 100 for every integer i with 0 <= i < len(nums).
